entities.name: Marjorie Stewart Joyner
entities.description: Chicago beautician, salon owner, Madam C. J. Walker Company executive (national supervisor of ~200 beauty schools, later vice president), inventor of the permanent wave machine (U.S. Patent 1,693,515, 1928); co-founder, United Beauty School Owners and Teachers Association (1945); drafter of Illinois cosmetology law.

entities.name: Annie Turnbo Malone
entities.description: Founder of the Poro system (Poro College, St. Louis, 1918); moved Chicago headquarters to the 'Poro Block,' 4415 S. Parkway, c. 1930.

entities.name: Anthony Overton
entities.description: Lawyer-turned-manufacturer; founder of Overton Hygienic (1898); moved company to Chicago 1911; builder of the Overton Hygienic Building; also a banker and newspaper publisher.

entities.name: George E. Johnson
entities.description: Co-founder of Johnson Products Company (Chicago, 1954); first Black-owned American Stock Exchange listing (1971); died July 6, 2026.

entities.name: Joan Henderson Johnson
entities.description: Co-founder of Johnson Products Company (1954); worked in the plant and offices through its growth.

entities.name: Edward Gardner
entities.description: Co-founder of Soft Sheen Products (Chicago, 1964); salon-first distribution; led 1983 voter-registration drive for Harold Washington.

entities.name: Bettiann Gardner
entities.description: Co-founder of Soft Sheen Products (1964); led manufacturing and operations.

entities.name: Madam C. J. Walker
entities.description: Founder of the Madam C. J. Walker Manufacturing Company; employer of Joyner; architect of the agent-school system that Joyner supervised.

entities.name: Oscar J. Freeman
entities.description: Chicago barber; owner of the Metropolitan Barber Shop, 4654 South Parkway; documented by the FSA-OWI in 1942 (14 years in business).

entities.name: Quincy T. Mills
entities.description: Historian; author of Cutting Along the Color Line: Black Barbers and Barber Shops in America (UPenn Press, 2013).

entities.name: Tiffany Gill
entities.description: Historian; author of Beauty Shop Politics; 'Civic Beauty,' Enterprise & Society.

entities.name: Z. Erol Smith
entities.description: Black architect of the Overton Hygienic Building (1922).

entities.name: Madam C. J. Walker Manufacturing Company
entities.description: Black-owned cosmetics manufacturer; beauty schools, agent network, conventions; patent-holder of Joyner's wave machine.

entities.name: Poro College / Poro Company
entities.description: Annie Malone's cosmetology school, manufacturer, and franchise-agent network; Chicago HQ from c. 1930.

entities.name: Overton Hygienic Manufacturing Company
entities.description: Black-owned cosmetics manufacturer (High-Brown products); Chicago from 1911; in business until early 1980s.

entities.name: Johnson Products Company
entities.description: Black-owned hair-care manufacturer, Chicago (1954–1993); Ultra Sheen, Afro Sheen; first Black-owned AMEX listing; Soul Train sponsor; sold to IVAX 1993.

entities.name: Soft Sheen Products, Inc.
entities.description: Black-owned hair-care manufacturer, Chicago (1964–1998); Care Free Curl, Optimum; salon-professional distribution; merged with Carson (1988), sold to L'Oréal (1998).

entities.name: S. B. Fuller Products
entities.description: Black-owned cosmetics company; George E. Johnson's employer and training ground before 1954.

entities.name: National Beauty Culturists' League (NBCL)
entities.description: Black beauticians' trade organization; originated 1919, chartered 1940; standards, education, legislation; addressed by MLK in 1957.

entities.name: United Beauty School Owners and Teachers Association
entities.description: Trade association founded 1945 by Marjorie Joyner and Mary McLeod Bethune.

entities.name: Metropolitan Barber Shop
entities.description: Barbershop at 4654 South Parkway, Chicago; owned by Oscar J. Freeman; documented 1942.

entities.name: Douglass National Bank
entities.description: Overton enterprise; tenant/shareholder of the Overton Hygienic Building (cross-ref CTL-RB-BIZ-000002).

entities.name: Overton Hygienic Building
entities.description: 3619–3627 S. State Street, Chicago (1922); housed cosmetics manufacturing, bank, insurance, professional offices; Black Metropolis–Bronzeville Historic District.

entities.name: Poro Block
entities.description: 4415 S. Parkway (now King Drive), Chicago; Poro Company Chicago headquarters from c. 1930.

entities.name: Joyner's salon (South State Street)
entities.description: Beauty salon opened by Marjorie Joyner c. 1916 on South State Street, Chicago; served clients of all races; exact address unrecovered.

entities.name: Metropolitan Barber Shop site
entities.description: 4654 South Parkway (now King Drive), Chicago; Oscar J. Freeman's shop, documented 1942.

entities.name: Binga Block barber shop
entities.description: Unnamed barber shop in the Binga Block, State Street between 47th and 48th, Chicago; documented in the IIT Bronzeville booklet.

entities.name: 63rd Street corridor
entities.description: South Side commercial corridor; Harrison's Barber Shop listed as provisional in CTL-DR-PLACE-001.

entities.name: Harrison's Barber Shop
entities.description: Barbershop on the 63rd Street corridor; named in CTL-DR-PLACE-001 but provisional pending directory work.

entities.name: Permanent wave machine
entities.description: Joyner's 1928 invention: 16 rods inside a drying hood; scalp protector added; rights held by the Walker Company; exhibited by the Smithsonian (1987).

entities.name: Ultra Sheen
entities.description: Johnson Products hair straightener; marketed to reduce hot-comb use and beauty-shop visits.

entities.name: Afro Sheen
entities.description: Johnson Products line marketed with 'Black is beautiful' messaging ('soul food for the natural').

entities.name: Care Free Curl
entities.description: Soft Sheen's Jheri Curl product (1981); sold only through professional cosmetologists.

entities.name: High-Brown face powder
entities.description: Overton Hygienic's early-1900s shade-range cosmetics line for Black women.

entities.name: Soul Train
entities.description: Television show; exclusive sponsor Johnson Products from 1971 (cross-ref CTL-DR-BMI-002 / CTL-DR-MUSIC-001).

entities.name: L'Oréal
entities.description: Acquirer of Soft Sheen (1998); endpoint of the Chicago Black-owned manufacturer consolidation arc.

entities.name: IVAX Corporation
entities.description: Pharmaceutical firm; acquirer of Johnson Products (1993) for ~$67M.

entities.name: Vivian G. Harsh Research Collection (Chicago Public Library)
entities.description: Reported holder of Marjorie Joyner's papers (lead; not verified).

entities.name: Illinois cosmetology licensing regime
entities.description: State licensing framework Joyner helped draft (date disputed); professionalization-as-uplift and as barrier to home-shop practitioners.
